_comment: Same steer_text transfer as text_rebase_t5base_t5large_steer_hubcheckpoint.json, but the target head is trained from scratch (linear_probe_head) instead of loaded from a nearest-mean-cosine file. Do NOT set target_task_heads alongside linear_probe_head, they're mutually exclusive.
_prepare_time_head_NOTE: steer_text's Stage 1 reads w_b off B's live head at prepare() time -- under linear_probe_head that's still B's from-scratch random init (the probe hasn't trained yet), not a real head. This is the accepted consequence of 'head initialized from scratch, then probed after rebasin': prepare()/transport() run first against the untrained head, the probe fits afterwards on top of whatever steer's correction produces.
_source_head: source_task_heads is NOT set on purpose: varun-v-rao/t5-base-snli already contains its own real fine-tuned classification_head.* weights, loaded automatically by TextLM.build when _load_tuned_source_state_dict detects the tuned_ckpts entry is a full Hub model -- steer_text.prepare() reads w_a straight off that live head.
_source_input_template: varun-v-rao/t5-base-snli was fine-tuned on a single formatted string, not this repo's default tokenizer(premise, hypothesis) pair encoding -- confirmed with scripts/probe_nli_input_format.py. This is A-only: B (t5-v1_1-large) still uses the default pair encoding.
_block_ridge_note: feature_regime=linear + stage_2_strategy=block_ridge groups B's 24 residual blocks down (block_group_strategy=concat) to match A's 12. The forward-mode jvp linearizes A (t5-base, ~220M params, 12 layers), NOT B.
